newsitem.title: ESTONIA: ESTONIA-ESTONIAN AIR TRAFFIC UP IN FIRST TWO MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: ESTONIA-ESTONIAN AIR TRAFFIC UP IN FIRST TWO MONTHS.

text.p: Estonian Air, majority owned by Danish Maersk, on Wednesday said that its passenger traffic on major routes to western Europe was up although routes to Helsinki were lower.
It said in a statement that traffic rose 50 percent on routes to Amsterdam, London and Copenhagen during the first two months compared with the same period in 1996.
It said a similar trend had been seen on the Tallinn to Moscow route but that traffic between Helsinki and Tallinn was "notably lower".
"Visa-free travel between Estonia and Scandinavia, which will be introduced in this spring, will in our opinion have a positive impact on air traffic," vice-president commercial, Toomas Leis, said.
The company flies to 10 destinations and has two Boeings and two Fokker 50s.
